g.text: Anatomy of a two-die GPU package (schematic)
① TOP VIEW - what sits on the package
② CROSS-SECTION - how the pieces are stacked (bottom to top = board to chips)

text.tspan: 8 HBM stacks · B200: 192 GB HBM3E at 8 TB/s (~1 TB/s per stack)
Rubin: 288 GB HBM4 at 19.2 TB/s (~2.4 TB/s per stack, 2,048-bit bus)
Transistors: B200 208B · Rubin 336B, both on two dies
Rubin Ultra (2027 roadmap): four compute dies, 16 HBM4E stacks, ~1 TB (two-die version reported)
Off-package links: NVLink SerDes (NVLink 5: 1.8 TB/s · NVLink 6: 3.0 TB/s per GPU)
and NVLink-C2C to the Grace / Vera CPU

g.text: Micro-bumps: tens of thousands of tiny solder joints

text.tspan: CoWoS-L interposer: redistribution layers + embedded local silicon bridges (LSI) carry die-to-HBM and NV-HBI wires
(B200 moved from CoWoS-S's single silicon interposer to CoWoS-L to span more than two reticles of silicon)

g.text: Organic package substrate (ABF build-up layers): fans power and I/O out to coarse pins
Board: HGX baseboard or Grace/Vera Superchip board; cold plate sits on top of the dies

text.tspan: half the SMs, L2 and HBM controllers
one address space, one CUDA device
HBM stack: 8-16 DRAM dies + base logic die
